#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""The record's tool: it owns the form of FACTS.md and POSITIONS.md and of
their two history files, and is the only way to write them.

An entry is one line under a permanent number, `- F-87 **Title.** Text.` in
explorations/coordinator/FACTS.md and `- P-48 **Title.** Text.` in
POSITIONS.md. A number is never reused or changed: a new entry takes the
highest number its file has ever used, plus one. An entry stands under the
nearest `## ` or `### ` heading above it, its section. Its title is its bold
opening, or where it has none, its opening words up to the first colon,
semicolon or full stop.

A pointer is another entry's number in the sentence that needs it, alone
(`It builds P-48.`) or with the first words of the target's title in quotes
(`It builds P-48, "A type parameter the arguments do not fix ..."`, or
`P-48 ("...")`). Quoted words must open the target's current title (`...` or
`…` marks words left out); when an entry is retitled, the tool rewrites them
in every entry that points to it, in the same call.

The history (FACTS-history.md, POSITIONS-history.md beside the record) holds,
under `### F-87`, one block per change, oldest first: one provenance line (the
UTC time from the clock, the kind of change, `from` each report section,
`commit`, `by`, then the note after a colon), and the line as it stood before
the change. The tool derives the kind: `added`, `rewritten`, `moved to "S"`,
`merged into F-n`, `F-n merged in`, `removed`; the numbering wrote one
`numbered` block per entry. A retitle that refreshed other entries' pointer
words, or a merge that moved their pointers, says so in one more line of the
block (`pointer words refreshed in: F-12, P-48`).

Every write takes a lock (flock on .record.lock beside the record), checks the
state it would leave, appends the history blocks first and then replaces each
record file in one step. A write is refused only for what would break the
store: a bad number, a pointer that does not resolve or whose words do not
open its target's title, a line break in an entry, no provenance (neither
`--from` nor `--note`). Never for size. The tool does not commit: commit the
record file and its history together.

usage: record.py COMMAND [ARGS] [PROVENANCE] [--root DIR]

  PROVENANCE: --from PATH#HEADING (repeatable; PATH from the repository root
  or from explorations/, HEADING held by exactly one heading of it, as doc:
  resolves one), --commit HASH (in HEAD's history), --by WHO, --note WHY.
  Each write needs --from or --note.

  add F|P --section TITLE FILE   a new entry from FILE's one line, numbered
      record.py add F --section 'Landed semantics' new.md --from 'compile-ladder/rung-x/REPORT.md#The fix' --by coordinator
  set N [FILE] [--section TITLE] entry N rewritten from FILE's line, or moved
      record.py set F-87 f87.md --from 'compile-ladder/rung-x/REPORT.md#The question' --note 'cut to the form'
  merge N --into M [FILE]        N removed, M rewritten from FILE (or kept),
                                 every pointer to N made a pointer to M
      record.py merge F-90 --into F-87 f87.md --note 'one fact, two entries'
  remove N                       N removed; refused while a pointer to it remains
      record.py remove P-131 --note 'evicted to the coordinator skill, references/briefing.md'
  apply FILE                     many changes from one file, all or none (below)
      record.py apply chunk3.md --by 'consolidation chunk 3'
  check [--base COMMIT]          the store's checks; exit 1 on a failure
      record.py check --base cc9424c2a

An apply file holds, in any order: `## TITLE` or `### TITLE`, the section the
new entries below it go to (an existing entry stands under no heading, or
under its own section's, or the `## ` one that holds it); entry lines as they
should stand, `- F-87 ...`, or `- F-?1 ...` for a new entry, its placeholder
replaced by its number everywhere in the file; `move F-87 to SECTION`;
`remove F-90`; `merge F-91 into F-87`. Each may be followed by one indented
provenance line of its own:
`  from: PATH, "HEADING"; commit: HASH; by: WHO; note: WHY`. Blank lines and

54:- P-55 **A size may hold arithmetic, compared by its written form once numerals are folded (item 15, 15a with (b)).** The checker accepts a sum, difference, product or power in a size. `2 3` folds to `6`, but `s0 s1` is not `s1 s0`. The class loader computes the value when it makes a class. A size name may equal a numeral, as the team's Q&A answers, so the `N[\0\]` arm of a `typecase N[\b0\]` is reachable. The library keeps the team's sizes written as products and sums. Two later array forks stand at defaults while his answers are pending: fork 3, a size known only at run time, at way 4a, where his reading of P-40 is asked; and fork 2, the bound of `Vector` and `Matrix`, at the two-trait bound (PLAN items 13 and 52).

72:- P-66 **The integer principle: Java's and the JVM's defaults stay where they make sense, and are corrected where they fail high performance or mathematical precision.** The team did so with rounding and the sign of `GCD`. A hardware behaviour that bytecode can express gets its own explicit spelling, as the specification's wrapping and saturating operators do. Where the JVM prevents a correct implementation, the project gives way for now. The peers to compare are Julia, X10, Swift and Rust.

## The goal

- P-7 **The goal is to finish what the designers intended, measured by one program, microGPT, compiled to bytecode and running fast.** The judge is `Specification/`, the Working Draft of February 2011 as the revival revises it, with the 2012 Types chapter cited beside it (P-25). The language is not redesigned. The specification is a living document that states the revival's changes (P-95). The floor to measure against is a pure-Java microGPT, not yet written (PLAN phase 6).
- P-8 **Where the designers left no word, he decides by the goal, a compiled microGPT running fast, not by type-theoretic purity, and stays true to the spirit of Fortress.** He accepts the language's unfinished corners rather than stall in theory. He has not read the specification, the type papers or the library, and takes the designers to have known more than he does. So a review checks his decisions against their intent, for errors of commission and of omission; its items are decisions in this file. Detail: `reviews/decisions-review/judgement.md`, "In short".
- P-9 **The search is for microGPT's most readable expression.** In his words, "we are searching for the optimal expression of the microGPT algorithm for readability." The two sources are Fortress's mathematical notation and Iverson's APL notation, with Hsu's data design for data-flow algorithms. The flat program in Hsu's style, C4, fell short, so polishing happens in the vocabulary, the operations the model is written in. C4 is the APL program's target form. Its hyperparameters are tuple bindings, the form an APL strand assignment expands to; the semicolon form of those lines is set aside.
- P-10 **The APL side quest is closed: its remaining ground, tacit functions, characters and nested arrays, is not pursued.** Its sub-language expands APL to Fortress code over native arrays, and its APL microGPT program stays in the walk check (P-30).
- P-11 **The 2D notation is a gimmick: no work on it unless he asks.** Fortify's mathematical rendering bakes one view of a computation into the syntax, though the same mathematics can be written many ways. APL's one glyph for each transformation does that better. It is presentation only, off the path, and no argument for Fortress.
- P-12 **The type checker on interpreter programs comes after the switch-over.** He wants the checker usable on the programs that walk runs, and sees it as low-hanging fruit. Today it checks only against the compiler's prelude (F-9). It comes once walk also takes the static coercions that the checker inserts (P-59).

## History he knows (do not re-explain)

- P-16 **He reads the project's end as the price of doing no work on performance.** DARPA's HPCS did not take Sun into its third phase in 2006, and the project went on at Sun Labs until 2012. The team worked on syntax, and the compiler that was to make the mathematical types fast never came; the funding was cut for good reason.
- P-17 **Unboxed doubles and arrays of doubles are required: without them the revival misses its point.** The code generator boxes every number, and boxing is the main cost on microGPT's array kernels (F-11). Boxing is measured on microGPT-shaped kernels, not on a scalar loop with literals and a `:=` accumulator, which microGPT never runs. The storage is P-84's decision; unboxed arithmetic is PLAN phase 6 (P-33).
- P-18 **He is coming round to Hsu's view that language paradigms are accidental complexity.**
- P-19 **The tree is not described as the third-party port's migration grafted on its history.** The files that still say so wait for the lineage cleanup (PLAN, "Off the path, parked"), which `coordinator/lineage.md`, "Files that still repeat it", lists. ### The standard and the sources

- P-25 **The specification stays the standard, the Types chapter beside it.** Where the Types chapter of the team's unfinished 2012 restart (F-166) covers a topic, it is cited beside `Specification/` as the designers' later word. On the rules that the revival revises, it is their latest intent, which the goal is to finish. It covers the exclusion rule, as instantiation exclusion in its two-part form, the `covariant` modifier, and `Bottom`, which no program can write.
- P-26 **The type group's late positions outweigh the specification's early text where they conflict.** The early text was a wish. The type group then made the language run, for performance and with specialization a must, and learned what is feasible. So their later word wins: the exclusion rule, specialization kept, the compiler prelude's tower flattened in 2009 and 2010 (P-43), Naden's 2012 write-up, the POPL 2019 paper. - P-27 **The library's own practice is the standard.** What microGPT invented goes into the standard library, in the library's own style. Whoever extends the library first studies how it does the same kind of thing, and follows that pattern; exclusion, for one, is all over it. So no performance decision of any kind, and no edit of C4, the flat model program, for speed, until microGPT runs compiled. The gate never runs the two microGPT programs, too long-running to be tests: it compiles them and records the phase that each reaches. A run of them, once possible, goes to a stage that does not gate.
